subject: ela
intro: This quiz checks your command of standard English pronoun grammar and usage: correct pronoun case, intensive pronouns, fixing shifts in number and person, and resolving vague pronouns. Each question includes the sentence or passage it depends on. Choose the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'My cousin and ___ rode our bikes to the park.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?
A) me
B) I
C) myself
D) him

steps: The blank is part of the compound subject 'My cousin and ___' that performs the action 'rode,' so a subjective-case pronoun is needed.
'I' is the subjective-case pronoun, so the correct answer is B.
A) 'me' is the objective case and cannot serve as a subject; saying 'me rode' is non-standard.
C) 'myself' is an intensive or reflexive pronoun and cannot replace the subject 'I.'
D) 'him' is objective and also changes the meaning, so it does not fit the subject slot.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The coach gave the trophy to Maria and ___ after the game.' Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?
A) I
B) she
C) me
D) myself

steps: The blank follows the preposition 'to' and is part of the compound object 'Maria and ___,' so an objective-case pronoun is needed.
'me' is the objective-case pronoun, so the correct answer is C.
A) 'I' is subjective case; 'to Maria and I' is a common overcorrection but is non-standard.
B) 'she' is also subjective case and cannot be the object of 'to.'
D) 'myself' is intensive or reflexive and cannot stand in for the object 'me' here.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The author herself signed every copy of the book at the event.' What does the word 'herself' do in this sentence?
A) It is an intensive pronoun that emphasizes the noun 'author.'
B) It is the direct object that receives the action 'signed.'
C) It is a possessive pronoun showing that the author owns the book.
D) It is the subject performing the action in the sentence.
items.answer: A) It is an intensive pronoun that emphasizes the noun 'author.'

steps: 'herself' sits right after the noun 'author' and adds emphasis without changing the basic meaning, which is the job of an intensive pronoun, so the answer is A.
B is wrong because the action 'signed' acts on 'every copy,' not on 'herself'; this is an intensive pronoun, not a reflexive object.
C is wrong because 'herself' shows no ownership; the possessive form would be 'her.'
D is wrong because the subject is 'The author'; 'herself' only emphasizes that subject.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'When a student forgets their homework, they should email the teacher right away.' Which revision best fixes the shift in pronoun number?
A) When a student forgets your homework, you should email the teacher right away.
B) When students forget their homework, they should email the teacher right away.
C) When a student forgets their homework, you should email the teacher right away.
D) When a student forgets their homework, they should email the teacher right away.
items.answer: B) When students forget their homework, they should email the teacher right away.

steps: The original mixes the singular 'a student' with the plural pronouns 'their' and 'they,' an inappropriate shift in number.
B fixes the agreement by making the noun plural ('students') so it matches the plural pronouns 'their' and 'they,' so B is correct.
A introduces a new shift, changing from third person ('a student') to second person ('your/you').
C also shifts to second person 'you' and still leaves the mismatch with 'a student.'
D simply repeats the original sentence and does not fix the singular-to-plural mismatch.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'If a runner trains every day, you will see steady improvement over the season.' Which revision best fixes the inappropriate shift in person?
A) If a runner trains every day, he or she will see steady improvement over the season.
B) If you train every day, a runner will see steady improvement over the season.
C) If a runner trains every day, they themselves will see steady improvement.
D) If a runner trains every day, you yourself will see steady improvement.
items.answer: A) If a runner trains every day, he or she will see steady improvement over the season.

steps: The sentence starts in the third person ('a runner') but shifts to the second person ('you'), an inappropriate shift in person.
A keeps the third person consistent by using 'he or she' to match 'a runner,' so A is correct.
B still mixes second person ('you') with third person ('a runner') and reverses the logic.
C adds the intensive 'themselves' and pairs the plural 'they' with the singular 'a runner,' creating a number error.
D keeps the second-person 'you' and adds 'yourself,' so the third-to-second person shift is not fixed.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'Carlos told Andre that he had been chosen for the team.' Why is this sentence unclear, and which revision fixes it best?
A) It is clear as written because 'he' refers to Carlos.
B) 'he' is vague because it could mean Carlos or Andre; revise to 'Carlos told Andre that Andre had been chosen for the team.'
C) The sentence needs a comma; revise to 'Carlos told Andre, that he had been chosen for the team.'
D) 'he' should be 'him'; revise to 'Carlos told Andre that him had been chosen for the team.'
items.answer: B) 'he' is vague because it could mean Carlos or Andre; revise to 'Carlos told Andre that Andre had been chosen for the team.'

steps: Two male names, Carlos and Andre, both come before 'he,' so the pronoun has two possible antecedents and the meaning is ambiguous.
B names the intended person ('Andre') in place of the vague 'he,' which removes the ambiguity, so B is correct.
A is wrong because the sentence is not clear; 'he' could just as easily mean Andre.
C is wrong because adding a comma does not clear up who 'he' is and creates a punctuation error.
D is wrong because 'he' is the subject of 'had been chosen' and must stay subjective; 'him had been chosen' is non-standard and still vague.

items.prompt:
Read the passage: 'Me and Jordan joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and I. Soon a student realized that they had built the fastest robot.' Which revision best follows standard English throughout?
A) Jordan and I joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and me. Soon a student realized that he or she had built the fastest robot.
B) Me and Jordan joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and me. Soon a student realized that you had built the fastest robot.
C) Jordan and me joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and I. Soon students realized that they had built the fastest robot.
D) Jordan and I joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and I. Soon a student realized that they had built the fastest robot.
items.answer: A) Jordan and I joined the robotics club last fall. The advisor gave the first toolkit to Jordan and me. Soon a student realized that he or she had built the fastest robot.

steps: The passage has three problems: a compound-subject case error ('Me and Jordan'), a compound-object case error ('to Jordan and I'), and a number shift ('a student' paired with 'they').
A fixes all three: subjective 'Jordan and I' as the subject, objective 'to Jordan and me' as the object, and 'he or she' to match the singular 'a student,' so A is correct.
B leaves the subject error 'Me and Jordan' and introduces a person shift to 'you.'
C uses objective 'Jordan and me' as a subject and subjective 'Jordan and I' as an object, reversing both case rules.
D corrects the subject but keeps the object error 'to Jordan and I' and still pairs the plural 'they' with the singular 'a student.'

items.prompt:
Read the passage: 'Nina and Priya share a locker near the gym. After practice, Nina handed Priya her water bottle and a towel. She thanked her quickly and hurried to class.' The sentence 'She thanked her quickly' is unclear. Based on the context, which revision states the meaning most clearly in standard English?
A) She thanked her quickly and hurried to class.
B) Priya thanked Nina quickly and hurried to class.
C) Her thanked she quickly and hurried to class.
D) Nina and Priya thanked themselves quickly and hurried to class.
items.answer: B) Priya thanked Nina quickly and hurried to class.

steps: Nina hands the water bottle and towel to Priya, so the natural meaning is that Priya, the person who received the items, thanks Nina, the person who gave them.
B replaces the vague 'She' and 'her' with the intended names 'Priya' and 'Nina' in the correct subjective and objective cases, so B is correct.
A is wrong because 'She' and 'her' each have two possible antecedents and stay ambiguous.
C is wrong because it swaps the cases, making the objective 'Her' a subject and the subjective 'she' an object, which is non-standard.
D is wrong because it changes the meaning, since neither girl thanks herself; the intensive or reflexive 'themselves' does not match the situation.
